Check your existing backups first. If Play App Signing is enabled, you can create a new keystore and request a lost upload key reset in Play Console using its PEM certificate. This leaves the app signing key held by Google unchanged. See the recovery section in Keystore Manager for the steps.

Reinstalling HTML to APK does not automatically restore your old key. If you previously saved a persistent copy, use Find backups on device in Keystore Manager. You can also import an exported .p12 file using its password and alias. Then check that the correct keystore is selected in your project.

Create your Google Play Console account and complete the identity and device checks required for your account type. New accounts have a one-time registration fee of US$25. Check the requirements shown in Play Console before publishing.

Set your project name, unique package name and icon. Use the target SDK level required by Google Play. Select AAB as the publishing format; this option requires Pro in our app. APK is for direct installation and sharing; new Google Play apps are published as AABs.

Keep your keystore file, passwords and key alias in a safe place. With Pro, you can export it as a .p12 file. Keep a separate copy on your computer or in secure cloud storage as well as any device backup. A PEM certificate alone cannot be used to sign an app.

Create your app in Play Console. Choose its name, default language and whether it is free or paid. Add a category, descriptions, icon, screenshots and contact details. The listing should accurately describe what your app offers.

Complete the content rating, target audience, ads, app access and Data safety sections. Include data practices of your HTML content, websites opened by the app and additional services such as advertising. If features require a login, provide the review team with the access details they need.

Every app needs a privacy policy, even if it collects no data. Add a publicly accessible policy link in Play Console and make the policy available inside your app. Describe your actual data practices, retention and deletion practices, and contact details. Keep it consistent with your Data safety declaration.

Upload your signed AAB to a testing track first and try the version installed through Google Play. For personal accounts created after November 13, 2023, applying for production access requires at least 12 testers continuously opted into a closed test for 14 days. Follow the current requirements shown for your account.

Complete the Play Console checklist and fix testing issues and errors that block publishing. If required, wait for your production access application to be approved, then submit the release for review. Review can take a few hours to 7 days, or longer in some cases. Track approval and publishing status in Play Console.

Keep the package name and increase the version code (versionCode) for every release. Sign the AAB with the upload key registered in Play Console. If the key changed, complete the reset process first. Test the update before publishing and use a staged rollout when available.

Uninstalling the app or clearing its data can erase keys stored only inside it. Check your backups first.

1. Restore an existing backup
Use Find backups on device in Keystore Manager, or import your exported .p12 file using its password and alias. Select that keystore in your project.

2. Without a backup, check Play App Signing
If enabled, Google protects the app signing key. You can reset a lost upload key:
• Create a new keystore and use Export .pem to get its certificate.
• Select your app in Play Console. On the Play App Signing page, request a reset in the Upload key certificate section.
• Submit the new PEM certificate. Wait for Google to confirm when the new key can be used.
• Keep the package name and increase the version code. Sign the AAB with the new keystore and upload it.

Existing users can continue receiving updates because the app signing key held by Google stays the same.

If Play App Signing is not enabled
Without the original signing key or a usable backup, you cannot update the same app. You must publish a separate app with a new package name; existing users do not move to it automatically.

PEM, P12 and PEPK are different
PEM is only a certificate, not a key backup. P12 contains the private key and must be kept safe. PEPK is for encrypted key transfer when Play Console requests it; it cannot recover a lost key. Import and export actions require Pro.

A default keystore is generated automatically. With Pro, you can use a custom keystore and export your key. Back up the file, passwords and alias before your first release; do not rely only on the copy inside the app.
A keystore holds the private key used to sign your app. With Play App Signing, you sign the AAB with your upload key; Google signs the app delivered to users with the app signing key it protects.
